title: Building Anvi'o Profiles and Interactive Viewer
author: James E Thornton Jr
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.kwpcxdn

steps.title: SSH into HPC
steps.instruction: Open a terminal and connect to the high‑performance cluster with: `ssh username@hpcocelote` (or `ssh hpc ocelote` as shown).

steps.title: Verify BAM files exist
steps.instruction:
Go to the BAM folder and list the files to confirm they are present:
```
cd /rsgrps/bh_class/username/read_recruit/bam
ls *.bam
```

steps.title: Transfer BAM files to local computer
steps.instruction:
From your local machine (Windows, macOS, or Linux) run:
```
scp username@sftp.hpc.arizona.edu:/rsgrps/bh_class/username/read_recruit/bam/*bam .
```

steps.title: Create sample‑ID list file
steps.instruction: Create a plain‑text file that contains one sample identifier per line and name it `SAMPLE_IDs` (e.g., using `touch SAMPLE_IDs && nano SAMPLE_IDs`).

steps.title: Prepare Docker environment (PC users)
steps.instruction:
If you are on Windows, move the downloaded BAM files to a folder inside `Documents`. Open the Docker Quickstart Terminal, navigate to that folder, run `pwd` to obtain the absolute path, then start the Anvi’o container with:
```
docker run --rm -v /full/path/to/files:/my_data -p 8080:8080 -it meren/anvio:latest
```
If a Docker session is already running, list containers with `docker ps` and terminate the unwanted one with `docker kill <container_id>`.

steps.title: Initialize (sort/index) each BAM file
steps.instruction:
Inside the Docker terminal (or any bash shell) run the following loop to create sorted, indexed BAMs:
```
for sample in $(cat SAMPLE_IDs); do
  anvi-init-bam $sample.bam -o $sample.i.bam
done
```
The output files (`*.i.bam`) are the indexed BAMs required for profiling.

steps.title: Profile each BAM file with anvi‑profile
steps.instruction:
For every indexed BAM, execute `anvi-profile` with at least the contigs database, an output directory, and a short sample name. Example:
```
anvi-profile -i SRR1647045.i.bam -c contigs.db \
  --output-dir Ocean1 \
  --sample-name Ocean1
```
Key optional flags (keep defaults unless you have a reason to change):
- `--min-contig-length 2500` (default; do not go below 1000).
- `--list-contigs` to preview discarded contigs.
- `--contigs-of-interest <file>` to limit profiling.
- `--min-mean-coverage 0` (default keeps all contigs).
- `--skip-SNV-profiling` to skip SNV detection.
- `--min-coverage-for-variability 10` (default 10X coverage required for variant calls).
- `--report-variability-full` to report every variant (use with caution).
- `--cluster-contigs` to enable automatic clustering for a single profile (not needed when you will merge later).
Repeat the command for every partner BAM (e.g., `SRR34443.i.bam`).

steps.title: Merge all profiles with anvi‑merge
steps.instruction:
After all samples are profiled, merge them:
```
anvi-merge */RUNINFO.cp -o SAMPLES-MERGED -c contigs.db
```
Default clustering uses Euclidean distance and Ward linkage. You can modify with `--distance <metric>` and `--linkage <algorithm>`. To skip hierarchical clustering use `--skip-hierarchical-clustering`; to force it despite >20 000 splits use `--enforce-hierarchical-clustering`. CONCOCT binning runs automatically; to disable it add `--skip-concoct-binning`.

steps.title: Download partner BAM files
steps.instruction:
From your local machine run:
```
scp username@sftp.hpc.arizona.edu:/rsgrps/bh_class/partners/read_recruit/*bam .
```

steps.title: Launch Anvi’o interactive viewer
steps.instruction:
Start the viewer for the merged profile:
```
anvi-interactive -p SAMPLES-MERGED/PROFILE.db -c contigs.db
```

steps.title: Visualize phylogram and adjust layers
steps.instruction: In the viewer, open the *Layers* tab, click the **Draw** button to render a circle phylogram. Use the zoom controls to change detail level, switch tree shape (circle/rectangular) and adjust tree radius or width. Modify layer settings (color, text, bar, intensity, normalization such as square‑root or log, min/max cut‑offs, height, margin) as desired. Multiple layers can be edited simultaneously with the multi‑selector at the bottom.

steps.title: Load CONCOCT bin collection and inspect bins
steps.instruction:
In the *Bins* tab click **Load bin collection**, choose **CONCOCT**. The interface will display the number of bins found. You can:
- Select bins to view constituent contigs.
- Rename bins, change their colors, or delete them.
- Sort bins by name, unit count, or completion/contamination estimates.
- View the list of contig names in a bin by clicking the unit‑count button.
- Save or load bin collections for later use.
Use right‑click → **Inspect** on any contig to see gene annotations (KEGG, Pfam) and run an on‑the‑fly BLAST if needed.

steps.title: Summarize results with anvi‑summarize
steps.instruction:
From the command line generate a summary of the merged profile and CONCOCT bins:
```
anvi-summarize -p SAMPLES-MERGED/PROFILE.db -c contigs.db -o SAMPLES-SUMMARY -C CONCOCT
```
